about.intro: Lectern edits reveal.js presentations visually. It loads your HTML file, renders it with the deck’s own reveal.js, and writes only the slides you changed back into the file — comments, indentation and untouched slides stay exactly as they were.
about.license: MIT licensed. reveal.js is © Hakim El Hattab and contributors, MIT licensed. Not affiliated with any presentation software vendor.

panel.notesPlaceholder: Speaker notes for this slide (shown in the reveal.js speaker view, press S while presenting).
panel.aiHint: Each note is a thread. Yellow = waiting, green = done (with the assistant’s reply). Click a note to add a comment — a green one turns yellow again; double-click a green note to dismiss it. Notes never show when presenting.
panel.htmlHint: Edit the <section> of the current slide. Changes apply as one undoable step.
panel.aiEmpty: No notes yet. Right-click the spot on a slide (or use the “Note for AI” button) and write what you want done there, e.g. “draw a whale here”.
panel.promptCopied: Prompt copied — paste it to Claude Code.
map.hint: Drag to reorder · drop under a slide to nest it · click a title or a section to rename
map.newSlideEnd: New slide at the end of the deck

map.inferredSection: Guessed from the deck — click to write it down
nav.dragStacked: Drag a stacked slide within its own stack, or use the HTML view to move it out.
tip.note: Right-click anywhere on the slide to leave a note for your assistant — it lands where you point, and it reads them from the file. (Double-click an empty spot does the same.)
tip.panels: The panels are hidden. Q brings them back, M opens the map, and holding space shows everything for a look.
tip.select: Drag to move it, the handles resize it, Esc lets go. Press Enter — or just start typing — to edit the words.
tip.stack: This slide has slides below it: ↓ goes down the stack, → goes on to the next one along.
tip.autosave: Saved as you go, straight into the .html file — no export step.
tip.map: Click a title to rename it, drag a card to reorder, or drop one under another to make it a sub-slide.
tip.room: That was the background — click it again for the other room.
